relationships.last_test: The 1935 printed Glasgow burgess register has been visually inspected. On 14 September 1795 John Glasgow, merchant, entered as husband of Helen, lawful daughter of James Smith, mason and burgess/guild brother (printed p.197, PDF207). On 1 July 1817 Alexander Glasgow, merchant in Wilson’s Court, Argyle Street, entered as eldest son of John Glasgow, merchant and burgess/guild brother (p.306, PDF316). On 3 May 1844 John Glasgow, merchant, entered as a younger son of John Glasgow, merchant and burgess/guild brother (p.450, PDF460). The first entry strongly identifies the maintained John-1348/Helen Smith household; the sons are supported comparisons with Alexander-971 and John-1355. The sons’ entries do not name their mother, and the three admissions must not be treated as a literal statement that all three men form one family. These are inspected published register transcriptions; the underlying manuscript admission registers are unread. Burke’s Visitation, vol.2, printed armorial section p.67 (PDF341), has now been read in the scan. It explicitly describes Alexander of Old Court, formerly Auchinraith, as eldest son of the late John Glasgow and Helen, daughter of James Smith, and grandson of Alexander Glasgow, merchant, and Agnes Monro of Edinburgh. The family passage was already quoted in the held biography; inspecting it is not discovery of a previously unknown grandfather name. The underlying Lyon matriculation remains unread. The FamilySearch citation X17D-67M was checked directly: John was born 13 October 1771 and christened 19 October 1771 at Barony, parents Alexander Glasgow and Mary Munro. The copied 3 December 1765 date attached to that same citation is wrong; no independent 1765 record was verified in this review. This corrects the source account, not the vital fields or later identity of either modern John profile.
relationships.next_test: Inspect the Lyon matriculation or an independent estate/merchant record connecting John and Helen Smith to the 1771 Alexander/Mary Munro household; resolve Agnes versus Mary and the competing Colinton identity before raising to Probable.
